Subject: SLA onboarding credits & phased rollover for BrightGrid

Emma —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Attached is a concise SLA + onboarding proposal so you and procurement can review the numbers quickly. Highlights below to make it easy: 

- Uptime tiers: 99.95% (Standard), 99.99% (Premier).
- Response windows (P1/P2/P3): 15 min / 1 hour / 4 hours for Premier; 1 hour / 4 hours / next-business-day for Standard.
- Escalation coverage: 24/7 P1 routing included on Premier; Standard includes business-hours escalation with optional on-call retainer.
- Onboarding credits: default 40 hours (applies to runbook/rollout help + initial optimization). I called out an optional 60/75 hour add-on in the attachment.
- Pricing concessions: 5% list discount at $250k TCV, 10% at $500k+.
- Phased rollover option: ramp committed capacity over three quarters (quarterly step-ups) with prorated billing during transition.

Quick asks so we can put this into a mutual action plan:
1) Confirm whether you prefer the 60 or 75 onboarding credit option (attachment shows cost impact).
2) Confirm desired SLA tier and whether phased rollover is required.
3) Procurement timing for DocuSign (we can prepare a redline-ready DocuSign envelope when you give the green light).

I've attached: Redwood_SLA_Proposal_BrightGrid_20281005.pdf and Onboarding_Credit_Schedule.xlsx.

If helpful, I can propose a one-page MA P (mutual action plan) once you pick the onboarding credit bucket — that will map dates for trial, canary, and full cutover.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference

Ben — thanks, got the proposal. A few follow-ups from our side: 

1) We are keen on a phased rollout: start with a 10% traffic canary for 30 days, then 50% for 60 days, then full. Can you confirm the pricing/prorate during those steps if we change committed capacity mid-contract?

2) Onboarding credits: would Redwood entertain a 60-day trial window and ~120 hours of onboarding credit for the canary and initial tuning? Our initial traffic spike will require hands-on tuning (prompt/ops). If there's a conversion to PS hours, please show hourly rates.

3) Procurement asked for SOC 2 artifacts and SLA redlines up front so they can move faster. Also need a target DocuSign timeline — would next-week signature be feasible if we align on credits now?

Forwarding procurement on this thread.

—Emma

Emma —

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers and a couple of options so procurement has choices: 

Prorate behavior (if you change committed capacity mid-term) — how we handle it: 
- Monthly prorate on committed capacity: changes take effect at the start of the following billing month. If you increase commitment mid-month, we bill incremental commit pro rata for remaining days. If you decrease, we credit pro rata for the remaining days.
- Credits earned for onboarding are consumed over the first 90 days by default; we can extend that burn window to 180 days for the higher-credit option.

Onboarding credit options (net impact shown in spreadsheet):
A) 60 hours — covers runbook + 2 optimization sessions.
B) 75 hours — priority hands-on tuning and 2 on-prem-ish cutover assists (recommended for fast ramp).
C) 120 hours — one-time larger engagement; converts to PS at $250/hr if unused (we can discount PS conversion by 15% for deals > $500k).

Trial window: we can extend to 60 days (from 30) without change to list pricing. For the 120-hour credit option we'll require a short SOW addendum to capture PS conversion terms.

Escalation/canary approach: we recommend the 10% canary for 30 days, then a 60-day 50% ramp, with a checklist sign-off for each step (ops readiness, e2e test pass). We will include a canary SLA that holds at Standard until final cutover to Premier if you elect the Premier tier.

Attached I included a redline starter (Redlines_BG.docx) where I tracked a few legal asks we typically see (prorate language, onboarding credit burn window, canary acceptance). Marissa — can you confirm whether the 75-hour onboarding credit and 60-day trial are approvable from a commercial standpoint? If so, I will turn this into a mutual action plan and generate the DocuSign envelope.

Emma — I'm attaching the SOC 2 packet link here (we keep a sanitized bundle we can share via secure link) and will drop a DocuSign draft next business day once Marissa signs off.

Ben
